text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Swedish state will receive up to 10 billion crowns rather than borrow in 1998 mainly due to higher tax revenue, the National Debt Office said. Wtihout this higher tax revenue the government would have to borrow between 15 and 25 billion crowns.

- Advertising on local television stations is doing better than ever. TV4's 16 stations have sold advertising space for 97.6 million crowns so far this year which is 61 percent higher than the same period last year. Industry spokesmen said this was largely due to new, improved technology.

- The number of drunk drivers has dropped dramatically since the mid-1980s with society being harder on these kinds of crimes and with the tolerance level lowered, according to a study by the newspaper.
- Medical technology company Elekta showed an bigger loss than expected on Wednesday of 38 million crowns. This made the share price plummet by 10 percent on the Stockholm bourse.

- Representatives of the Federal Reserve Bank in New York participated in the board of directors meeting of S-E-Banken in Stockholm on Monday. The Swedish bank's top managers explained how they have tightened controls on their American operation in an attempt to placate the regulators and avoid penalty fees.

- Sweden's decision to start closing its 12 nuclear reactors from next year has little support. A SIFO survey finds 54 percent of 1,000 people polled said economic and security considerations should determine when the plants are phased out, not environmental.

- Sweden's second largest shoe store chaim, Wedins, is to be listed in Stockholm on July 1. The 100-year-old company, which is owned by KF Invest and the Hegard family of Norway, plans to use the 50 million crowns they will raise to expand, opening new stores and making acquisitions.
